newsitem.title: USA: Teltrend shares drop after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Teltrend shares drop after profit warning.

text.p: Shares of Teltrend Inc fell almost 24 percent on Wednesday after the company warned that its second-quarter profit would fall short of earnings a year earlier and at least one analyst cut his rating on the stock.
"Basically their business in December all but dried up," said Greg Mesniaeff, an analyst for Robinson-Humphrey.
Mesniaeff cut his short-term rating to market perform from buy and lowered his earnings estimates on the company. He maintained his long-term buy recommendation.
Late Tuesday, Teltrend said it expected to report lower sales and earnings for its fiscal second quarter ending January 25 compared with year-ago levels. It did not provide specific estimates.
Before the warning, analysts on average were forecasting second-quarter earnings of $0.49 a share, according to a First Call survey.
Last year, Teltrend, which sells transmission equipment to telephone companies, posted earnings of $0.41 a share and sales of $20.5 million.

Mesniaeff said he had expected Teltrend to say its business with U S West Communications Group failed to pick up. But the company's business with all regional Bell operating companies, except for BellSouth Corp, has been slack, he said.

Chandan Sarkar, an analyst with SoundView Financial Group, said he viewed the Teltrend's current difficulties as "structural, not fundamental," reflecting the regional companies' efforts to reorganize their businesses. He believes the problem would correct itself by the end of the year.
Teltrend's key business -- T1 repeaters used to allow telephone lines to carry more data -- remains solid, he said.

By early afternoon, shares of Teltrend were off 5-1/2 at 17-1/2, rebounding during the session from 15-3/4, a 52-week low. Trading volume was more than 2.1 million, compared with a daily average of about 72,000. On Tuesday, the shares fell 2-3/4.

"We think the stock is a screaming buy down here below $20," Sarkar said. "We think the January quarter will be the worst, with some mild improvement in April and then a much stronger rebound in July."
